name: Kratom
description: Leaf of a Southeast Asian tree (Mitragyna speciosa) with over 50 alkaloids, mainly mitragynine

note.text: FDA says so. Controlled studies mostly tested safety, blood levels and abuse potential, not mood or anxiety treatment.

bullets: **Mitragynine and 7-OH** bind mu-opioid receptors, as opioid drugs do (FDA)
**7-OH** is more potent at that receptor than mitragynine and morphine
**Mitragynine** also acts on serotonin, dopamine and kappa-opioid systems
**In people,** doses of 3 g or more narrowed the pupils, an opioid-like effect
Small controlled safety and abuse studies
No trials as a treatment for mood or anxiety

practical.routes: By mouth (leaf powder, drinks, pure mitragynine)
practical.pharmacokinetics: Limited human data; 7-OH is also formed from mitragynine in the body
practical.soldAs: Unapproved products; FDA says not lawful as supplement or food
practical.monitored: Side effects, abuse-related effects, withdrawal, liver enzyme
practical.sport: Not named on the 2026 list; S0 status not stated

regulatory.text: Not approved; not lawful as supplement or food
3 related compounds Schedule I since Aug 2026

references: DEA, Federal Register 2026-20943, 7-OH above a threshold, Oct 14, 2026
